accept.why: As One's (owner, q153: match One): a word to peek at is the word's own width and 36 pt tall, with One's 4-pt hit slop (apps/heartseed/src/sayit/draw.tsx, Peek)

The web's alone, as One's: the web has no accessibility text sizes (Exact's accessibilityTextSize is false there), so at verify's 53-px root it keeps One's fixed 132-pt round button (apps/heartseed/src/sayit/draw.tsx, BigButton), whose label runs past the circle as One's reference cuts it. On iOS, at AX1 and up, Listen is a capsule the line's width that holds its label (owner, q160; tools/drive-largest.ts ios), and verify ios finds no spill there without this entry (hs-ax-better round 1)

As One's on iOS at the largest text: Appearance's three choices share one row of equal cells that never wraps (apps/heartseed/src/appearance/choice.tsx: group row, radio flex 1), so the words cannot all fit; the port's last choice runs 2 pt past the side (hs-largest round 1)

The web's measure, not a spill: the licences keep their spaces as One's text does (white-space pre-wrap), and Chrome's text range counts the space that hangs past a wrapped line's end; with the spaces collapsed (pre-line) the same check finds nothing, and verify ios finds no licence at the largest text (hs-largest round 1)

The web's alone, as One's: the web has no accessibility text sizes (Exact's accessibilityTextSize is false there), so at verify's 53-px root it keeps One's 34-pt title scaled by the text size (apps/heartseed/src/sayit/draw.tsx, title; src/first/intro.tsx, Intro's heading), and the one word Heartseed (106 px) is wider than any line of a 390-wide phone; the port wraps between words only, as verify's fixed-type check asks, so that word runs past its line there. The first minute's other headings wrap between their words; verify ios's leg at AX5 is owed to the sweep (par-hs-first round 1)
